findings.reason: if the plan reuses `_session_host_runs_follower` (the reader its own dispatch already trusts and that predates the marker) it may not need the new `/proc` predicate at all, and must at minimum say why that reader cannot be used.
findings.text: §15 proposes a new predicate to answer "is this follower the host's own child" from the owner stamp plus a `/proc` ancestor-argv walk, and cites neither the host census record that `SessionHost.record()` writes (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:308`, `children[].pid`) nor its reader `_session_host_runs_follower` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:477`), which the codebase already calls "what tells a host's follower from a hand-armed one" (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1210-1211`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:859`); the census writer landed with §4 at `87cc79c61` and so predates the reverted marker, meaning it survives the very incident that forced the revert (an old-code host lists its own child's pid), and the plan's own cited pair does not close the gap the plan claims — `_current_and_ancestor_argvs` returns this process's ancestor argv with no pids, so it cannot tie a "crew host" reading to the resolved owner

findings.reason: one of the two should be extended or removed; the plan should name `_session_host_runs_follower` as the owner to extend rather than adding a second reader beside it.
findings.text: a predicate built on the owner stamp and an ancestor argv read is a second, parallel state reader of the host-child question whose owner is `_session_host_runs_follower` (with the record it reads, `reckon/crew/session_host.py:308`), so §15 would leave two mechanisms that disagree the moment the census and the `/proc` reading diverge

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §15 adds one predicate inside existing modules (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py`) and introduces no new module or surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the predicate §15 adds is a second reader of a question the codebase already owns, the host census state read by `dispatch_watch._session_host_runs_follower`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1597, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §15 states it "adds one predicate and no public definition", re-adds neither the `CHILD_ENV` constant nor `RECKON_SESSION_HOST_CHILD` (grep confirms both absent), and adds no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §15 searches for a way to tell a host's own follower from a hand-armed one and cites the owner stamp (`session_host._spawn`), `runs.follower_owner()` and the `/proc`-walking `dispatch_watch._current_and_ancestor_argvs`/`runs._process_start_time`, but cites none of the machinery the codebase already uses for exactly this question — the host census record and `dispatch_watch._session_host_runs_follower`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §15 adds behaviour (the hand-off predicate and the end-of-line text it selects), not a pass-through layer over existing machinery, so there is no wrapper needing a justification.
